title: Starting up: project canvas and starting up workshops
blurb: Explain how starting up a project works in an agile setting, and match each topic to the project canvas workshop or the starting up workshop.
question: In starting up a project, a group brainstorms one to three key user groups and agrees a project vision. Which workshop is this, and what does the starting up workshop cover instead?

teach.body: Starting up a project is triggered by the project mandate and checks whether the project is viable and worthwhile. In PRINCE2 Agile the work is shaped around two workshops: the project canvas workshop and the starting up workshop. The project manager defines who takes part in each, sets the dates and invites the participants. The process stays light: just enough to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.

head: Activity
What happens
rows: Review similar projects; lessons log if useful
Executive leads the project canvas; PM creates the project backlog
Choose delivery solution; note tailoring needs
High-level release map for initiation; risks; controls
teach.caption: Paraphrased from Table 13.1.

teach.body: Its purpose is a shared understanding and a clear foundation for the agile project, by defining the project's core elements in line with organizational goals and priorities. Participants identify key user groups, evaluate business options, agree a project vision and analyse benefits and risks. The project executive leads the development of the project canvas from the mandate.

head: Topic
Typical work
rows: One to three key user groups, ranked
teach.caption: Table 13.2, paraphrased.

teach.body: The starting up workshop turns the canvas into a plan for initiation. Its topics are project roles (align on the team and role descriptions), lessons review (small groups gather lessons from earlier initiatives and their impact), initiation stage planning, risk analysis (threats and opportunities affecting initiation and the project) and refine planning (update the initiation stage plan and documents). The project backlog with epics is created here, and the release map is updated.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.3, Table 13.1

teach.h: Canvas workshop or starting up workshop?

teach.body: Larkspur Housing's mandate asks for an online repairs portal for tenants. Executive Grace Obi leads the canvas workshop: the group ranks tenants, contractors and call-centre staff as user groups, agrees a vision and lists scope as MoSCoW-ranked epics. Project manager Hamid Rahimi then runs the starting up workshop with CPO Elena Novak and senior supplier Mark Doyle: roles are agreed, lessons from an earlier portal are reviewed, and the initiation plan and release map are refined.

teach.text: The executive LEADS the project canvas; the PM, consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive, CREATES the project backlog. The daily log is created in starting up (appoint the executive and PM), not in initiation. And user groups, vision and scope belong to the canvas workshop, not the starting up workshop.

items: Starting up: viable and worthwhile? Kept light; triggered by the mandate.
PM sets participants, dates and invitations for both workshops (13.2.3).
Canvas workshop: user groups, options, vision, benefits, risks, scope, cost, value.
Starting up workshop: roles, lessons review, initiation planning, risk analysis, refine planning.
Executive leads the canvas; PM creates the project backlog with epics.
Plan the initiation stage gives a high-level release map for initiation.

summary: You can now describe starting up a project in an agile setting and tell the project canvas workshop topics from the starting up workshop topics. You also know who leads the canvas and who creates the project backlog.

A.q: In starting up a project, who leads the development of the project canvas from the project mandate?
A.why: In 'prepare the outline business case', the project executive leads the team in developing the project canvas from the mandate (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: The PM creates the project backlog, consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive.
whyNot.1: The CPO is consulted on the project backlog; the executive leads the canvas.
whyNot.3: The senior supplier is consulted on what the project will deliver.

A.q: Which topic of the starting up workshop has small groups gather lessons from previous initiatives and outline their impact?
A.why: The lessons review topic gathers lessons from earlier projects and initiatives (Table 13.3).

whyNot.1: Project roles aligns the team on the project management team and role descriptions.
whyNot.2: Risk analysis covers threats and opportunities for initiation and the project.
whyNot.3: Refine planning updates the initiation stage plan and documents.

A.q: In which starting up activity does the project manager create the daily log?
options: Appoint the executive and project manager
A.why: The PM creates the daily log in 'appoint the project executive and project manager' (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: Assessing previous lessons may create the lessons log, not the daily log.
whyNot.1: Planning the initiation stage produces the high-level release map for initiation.
whyNot.2: The outline business case activity produces the project canvas and project backlog.

B.q: Which is a topic of the project canvas workshop?
B.why: User group definition, with one to three ranked key user groups, is a canvas workshop topic (Table 13.2).

whyNot.0: The team skill matrix is a project kickoff workshop topic.
whyNot.2: Iteration planning belongs to the team planning workshop.
whyNot.3: OKR definition belongs to the release planning workshop.

B.q: Which topic of the project canvas workshop explores long-term outcomes so the project aligns with business value and sustainability objectives?
B.why: Project vision definition brainstorms long-term outcomes and produces a shared vision aligned with value and sustainability (Table 13.2).

whyNot.0: Benefits analysis lists benefits and dis-benefits and sets tolerances.
whyNot.1: Scope definition sets the timeline, tolerances and MoSCoW-ranked epics.
whyNot.2: User group definition ranks the key user groups.

B.q:
Which two statements about starting up a project are correct?
1. The project backlog with epics is created in the starting up workshop.
2. Persona definition is a topic of the project canvas workshop.
3. Assembling the project brief includes dependencies on other projects or activities.
4. The project manager leads the development of the project canvas.
B.why: The project backlog including epics is created in the starting up workshop (Tables 13.1, 13.3), and the project brief records dependencies (Table 13.1).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: persona definition is a project initiation workshop topic.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: personas belong to initiation, and the executive leads the canvas.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the project executive leads the canvas.

C.q: Which workshop has a 'risk analysis' topic on threats and opportunities affecting the initiation stage, and which process does it support?
options: Agile enablement workshop; directing a project
Project initiation workshop; initiating a project
Starting up workshop; starting up a project
Release planning workshop; managing a stage boundary
C.why: The starting up workshop's risk analysis looks at threats and opportunities that may affect initiation and the project (Table 13.3).

whyNot.0: The agile enablement workshop looks at risks to agile adoption from the Agilometer.
whyNot.1: The project initiation workshop covers the Agilometer, approaches, DoR, DoD and personas.
whyNot.3: Release planning covers OKRs and the release map for the next stage.

C.q: The PM, consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive, defines what the project will deliver. Which artifact is created, and in which activity?
options: Product backlog; plan the initiation stage
Project backlog; prepare the outline business case
Release map; assemble the project brief
Project canvas; select the project approach
C.why: In 'prepare the outline business case', the PM creates the project backlog after consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: Product backlogs hold a team's user stories; they are not created at this point.
whyNot.2: The brief records objectives, scope and dependencies; the release map comes from planning initiation.
whyNot.3: The canvas is led by the executive, in the outline business case activity.

C.q: In 'plan the initiation stage', what does the project manager produce, and with whom?
options: A high-level release map for initiation, with key stakeholders
A team plan for the first iteration, with the product owner
The project initiation documentation, with the board
A refined product backlog, with the developers
C.why: The PM identifies time and cost constraints for initiation and, with key stakeholders, produces the high-level release map for initiation (Table 13.1).

whyNot.1: Team plans are produced by delivery teams in managing product delivery.
whyNot.2: The PID is built during initiating a project, not when planning it.
whyNot.3: Product backlog refinement is a team planning workshop topic.

reteach.title: Planning a community festival
reteach.question: How do the two starting up workshops look if you are planning a town festival?

blocks.h: First the idea, then the planning team
blocks.body: The first meeting agrees who the festival is for, what it should achieve and roughly what is in and out: that is the canvas workshop. The second meeting agrees who does what, what went wrong at last year's fair, what could go wrong now and how the next planning month will run: that is the starting up workshop.

blocks.text: User groups and vision are canvas topics; roles and lessons review are starting up workshop topics.

explain.body: Starting up has activities from appointing the executive and PM (daily log) to planning initiation (release map for initiation). The project brief gathers objectives, scope, exclusions, tolerances, constraints, assumptions and dependencies.

test.q: Which activity confirms the objectives, scope, exclusions, tolerances, constraints, assumptions and dependencies?
test.why: Assembling the project brief confirms and documents these items (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: The outline business case produces the project canvas and project backlog.
whyNot.1: The approach activity evaluates delivery solutions.
whyNot.2: Planning initiation produces the release map for initiation and its controls.

explain.body: The project canvas workshop builds a shared understanding of the project's core elements in line with organizational goals: user groups, business options, vision, benefits, risks, scope, cost and business value.

test.q: What is the purpose of the project canvas workshop?
options: To agree team values, norms and team dashboards
To build a shared understanding of the project's core elements
To review Agilometer results with the board and coaches
To plan the next stage and define the team OKRs
test.why: It creates a shared understanding and clear foundation by defining the project's core elements in line with organizational goals (13.2.4.1).

whyNot.0: Values, norms and team dashboards are project kickoff topics.
whyNot.2: Reviewing the Agilometer with the board is the agile enablement workshop.
whyNot.3: OKRs and next stage planning belong to the release planning workshop.

explain.body: After roles, lessons, initiation planning and risk analysis, the refine planning topic updates the initiation stage plan in line with the agreed risk responses and updates the documents; the release map is updated.

test.q: Under which starting up workshop topic is the initiation stage plan updated once risk responses are agreed?
test.why: Refine planning updates the initiation stage plan and earlier documents; the release map is updated (Table 13.3).

whyNot.0: Initiation stage planning first develops what initiation needs; refining follows the risk analysis.
whyNot.1: Project roles aligns the team on roles.
whyNot.3: Lessons review gathers lessons from earlier initiatives.

explain.body: In starting up, the project manager defines the participants for the project canvas and starting up workshops, sets the dates and invites everyone. The executive leads the canvas content.

test.q: Who defines the participants for the project canvas and starting up workshops, sets the dates and invites everyone?
test.why: In starting up, the project manager defines participants, sets dates and invites them (13.2.3).

whyNot.1: The executive leads the canvas content but does not organize the workshops.
whyNot.2: The agile coach supports agile adoption; organizing these workshops is the PM's task.
whyNot.3: Project support may help with admin, but the book gives this task to the PM.
